>   private def innerAllowedInstrumentsBasedOnCorporateProfile(
>     corporateProfile: Option[CorporateProfileData],
>     maybeTradingAccountType: Option[TradingAccountType],
>     maybeGoalType: Option[InvestmentGoalType],
>     instruments: Seq[InstrumentInfoV2Dto],
>     maybeFromInstrumentIds: Option[Set[String]],
>     instrumentCache: LocaleAwareInstrumentCache,
>     productLine: ProductLine,
>     maybeLocale: Option[Locale]
>   ): Future[(Seq[InstrumentInfoV2Dto], Map[String, Set[InvestmentGoalType]])] = {
>     val baseInstruments = filterBaseInstruments(instruments, maybeFromInstrumentIds)
> 
>     val rules = corporateProfile.flatMap(profile => profile.configuredRules.get(productLine)).getOrElse(List(UnRestricted))
>     val baseInstrumentIds = baseInstruments.map(_.id).toList
>     val eligibleInstrumentsResponse = corporateProductRuleInterpreter.calculateEligibleInstrumentIds(
>       maybeTradingAccountType = maybeTradingAccountType,
>       maybeGoalType = maybeGoalType,
>       rules = rules,
>       availableInstrumentIds = baseInstrumentIds
>     )
>     val allEligibleInstrumentIds = eligibleInstrumentsResponse.eligibleInstruments
>     val eligibleInstrumentIds = maybeFromInstrumentIds
>       .map(allEligibleInstrumentIds.intersect)
>       .getOrElse(allEligibleInstrumentIds)
>     val added = eligibleInstrumentIds -- baseInstrumentIds
>     val locale = maybeLocale.getOrElse(Locale.defaultLocaleByRegion(region))
>     for {
>       newInstruments <- instrumentCache.getCachedInstruments(instrumentIds = added, locale = locale, withMstarDocs = false).map(_.values)
>       finalList = baseInstruments.filter(i => eligibleInstrumentIds.contains(i.id)) ++ newInstruments
>     } yield (finalList, eligibleInstrumentsResponse.exclusiveInstruments)
>   }

>   private def filterBaseInstruments(
>     instruments: Seq[InstrumentInfoV2Dto],

>         case Some(innerAccByTradingAccountType) =>
>           Some(innerAccByTradingAccountType.updatedWith(tradingAccountType) {
>             case Some(accumulatedFee) => Some(accumulatedFee + fee)
>             case None                 => Some(fee)
>           })
>         case None =>
>           Some(Map(tradingAccountType -> fee))
>       }
>   }
> ```

> The risk of what you said is there, but:
> 
> * We already retry \(I’ll change to retry for both exception type, only skip if sth else unexpected\)
> * Most of the time, the 2 sources match. Only for some rare cases, they have disparity
> * And the thing is, sometimes indeed MStar remove newest docs. It could be their mistake but it’s easier for us to follow them and raise to MStar to correct their data, instead of us trying to maintain something we don’t own \(I think\)
> 
> ‌
> 
> Ideally, I would want to capture the fact that sth fails and we fallback as well, i.e.
> 
> * if both sources succeed, we merge and trust MStar 100%
> * if one fails, we fallback to empty and still use the other successful one, but we won’t trust 100% and maybe log error to check

And worst is it’s not consistent, empty payload can be retried and can give valid xml later. So we can’t be for sure.
> 
> ‌
> 
> I think for first cut, let’s go with this and we monitor more across the daily runs to see if we can improve further.
> 
> ‌

> ‌

> goalEntityLoader(customerId, maybeGoalId): Future[Map[GoalId, Option[GoalDto]]]
> planEntityLoader(customerId, maybeGoalId, maybePlanId): Future[Map[PlanId, Option[PlanDto]]]
> ```
> 
> For the purpose of this PR, we would need `planEntityLoader` returning PlanDto instead
> 
> ‌
> 
> The maybeGoalId / maybePlanId should not be used to filter the returned entries, not interfering with actual data.
> 
> If we ever need to support finding GoalDto but filtering with planId, it should probably look sth like this
> 
> ```scala
> goalEntityLoader(customerId, maybeGoalId, maybeGoalPredicate): Future[Map[GoalId, Option[GoalDto]]]
> ```
> 
> The predicate can be anything based on goal data, but it must not modify the returned goal in any way

## A1-0868 — Standalone model separates automatic attributes from forced override and early deeplink validation

**Source stance:** explanation

**Context:**

> component: None; operation: [INV-4869] feat(bff, advisory, instrument, portfolio): Add a flag for instruments which are marked as Standalone-only and add amount restriction in fund-smart invest flow summary; trigger: Source-specific review condition as stated in the exact comment below.

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Just to summarize a bit so that we’re on the same page.
> 
> ‌
> 
> We have 2 levels of logic to determine if a fund is a standalone fund:
> 
> * derived logic based on fund attributes \(i.e. semi-liquid, redemption regulations, lots size, non-daily schedule\)… these are “rules” to auto qualify funds as standalone, without Ops having to configure anything
> * a “forced” flag to explicitly set a fund as standalone, even if they don’t check any of the above boxes… e.g. large NAV funds
> 
>   
> On `InstrumentInfoDto` \(static configuration of instrument data\), as of current PR, FE will only see the forced flag, but not the derived one. Hence on advisory instrument-list / instrument-details endpoints, BE would resolve both of the above and send a single resolved flag to FE to tell if a fund is effectively a standalone or not. This way FE can implement UX logic to guide customer for fund selection, so all that is good.
> 
> ‌
> 
> If customer lands on a deeplink with TAA to portfolio summary screen \(i.e. bypassing FE guardrails on fund selection\), we need to tell FE if such TAA is valid or not:
> 
> * if we handle everything properly, we would need to return it as warning/block flags at instrument level, so that FE can display properly \(similar to HK\)
> * but since we agreed to descope this piece \(i.e. no FE display\), we want to ensure at least such request is blocked as early as possible, not allowing customer to continue all the way to OTP and then get 5xx error
> 
> This eager block can be a simple flag in portfolio summary response, and FE can handle \(error or proper failure popup with explanation\). Or we can go with generic BadRequest as well. This is up to yall to discuss.
> 
> ‌
> 
> Another approach is to serialize the resolved isStandaloneFund flag in `InstrumentInfoDto` as a derived field as well \(i.e. not part of constructors, no setter, but part of json\). Then we leave it completely to FE to check the individual instruments' flag and handle.

**Conditions and limits:**

- Context component is inline_path metadata; operation is the exact PR title quoted separately from comment evidence.
- Derived semi-liquid, redemption regulation, lot size, nondaily schedule; early flag/BadRequest or JSON-only derived InstrumentInfoDto field proposed; OTP-late 5xx unacceptable.

## A1-1350 — New recurring schedule fix must not classify changed funding type as increase

> component: advisory-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/advisory/impl/productline/planupsert/sg/SgPlanUpsertSubmitForApprovalBehaviour.scala; operation: Fix and handle increase recurring schedule when there is no existng schedule; trigger: Source-specific review condition as stated in the exact comment below.

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Scenarios:
> 
> * contain one time -> ONE\_TIME\_INVESTMENT
> * stop recurring -> STOP\_RECURRING\_INVESTMENT
> * no recurring changes -> None
> * new recurring \(no existing\) -> before None >>> now INCREASE\_RECURRING\_INVESTMENT \(wanted fix\)
> * update recurring, same type with increasing amount -> INCREASE\_RECURRING\_INVESTMENT
> * update recurring, same type with decreasing amount -> DECREASE\_RECURRING\_INVESTMENT
> * update recurring, different type \(regardless of amount\) -> before None >>> now INCREASE\_RECURRING\_INVESTMENT \(unwanted fix\)
> 
> ‌
> 
> Either we introduce new types for last scenario \(which is not really built for B2B yet\), or we keep it as None

## A1-1407 — Do not use missing CPF/SRS firm fee config as FE toggle

**Source stance:** requested-change

**Context:**

> component: None; operation: Feat/BB-2642 bff retrive cpf srs fee detail; trigger: Source-specific review condition as stated in the exact comment below.

**Concern stated in the source:** All account ranges required at onboarding; missing config data issue; account linking still supported

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Fee range must be configured for all trading accounts at the point of firm onboarding. Missing config for CPF/SRS should be treated as data/setup issue, and we must not use it as FE feature toggle.
> 
> * Linking/displaying account should be supported regardless of existence of fee range config
> * Add goal flow can be changed to fail instead of fallback to empty fee range, so that FA can escalate
> 
> ‌
> 
> Moreover, current impl is too fragile:
> 
> * Data is returned in full shape. Should a customer be able to view such config of the firm, even if they belongs to same firm?
> * No RBAC / No ownership guards: once authenticated, anyone can call the endpoint by providing a customerId. Think customer/fa of Firm X calling the endpoint with customerId of Firm Y
> 
> ‌
> 
> We shouldn’t need this endpoint for this purpose of show/hide CPF/SRS features in FE \(at least not driven by missing data\).
> 
> If any, this endpoint is only useful when we want to display/manage firm’s fee range config in Advisor Portal, by PartnerOps or some super-FAM \(as opposed to manually controlled by Endowus Ops\)
> 
> When such requirement comes, we would still need proper RBAC resource for this tenant level data \+ new CanActionForTenantGuard
> 
> CC

**Conditions and limits:**

- Context component is inline_path metadata; operation is the exact PR title quoted separately from comment evidence.
- Current endpoint leaks full firm config without RBAC/ownership across firms; future management needs tenant RBAC and CanActionForTenantGuard.

## A1-1461 — Remove live full-redemption recheck from invalid-order replay handling

**Source stance:** requested-change

**Context:**

> component: trading-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/trading/impl/entities/plan/processors/PlanTraderProjection.scala; operation: [INV-4562] feat(charge, redemption, trading): Automate fee handling; trigger: Source-specific review condition as stated in the exact comment below.

**Concern stated in the source:** Cmd already established no full redemption; later live request must not suppress processing or alerts and leave trade stuck

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> If we want additional check, then we need to think about our future reader:
> 
> * One who follows the code would see that the cmdHandler already checks for ongoing full redemption, and that if `INVALID_ORDERS_GENERATED_BY_FEE_CHARGE` is thrown, that cmdHandler already validates there is no ongoing full redemption trade in the PlanTraderEntity
> * Now in projection, we again query again, but this time we check on redemption svc. This query is also live at the point of projection processing the event \(which can be replayed\), so it’s very possible that at this point, there is full redemption returned here
> * Then this code simply goes to do nothing and return
> 
> ‌
> 
> There would be 2 wrong things in such scenarios:
> 
> * The live full redemption request \(from redemption svc\) at this point should not have any effect on this processing logic
> * This fee redemption trade would be stuck due to invalid orders, and we do not have any alerts at all
> 
> ‌
> 
> I’d suggest to remove this check, unless we know there’s some corner cases that might happen
> 
> ‌

**Conditions and limits:**

- Context component is inline_path metadata; operation is the exact PR title quoted separately from comment evidence.

> 
> Is it better to resolve this upfront instead?
> 
> ‌
> 
> We can define `blacklistedInvestorTypes` as generic param, and move the logic to base builder `FundSmartInstrumentBuilder`
> 
> ```scala
>   protected def customTradingAccountTypeOrdering: Ordering[TradingAccountType]
> 
>   protected def getAllowedTradingAccountTypes(instrument: InstrumentInfoDto, blacklistedInvestorTypes: Set[InvestorType]): List[TradingAccountType] = {
>     instrument.tradingConfigDetails.allowedInvestorTypes
>       .filterNot(blacklistedInvestorTypes)
>       .flatMap { investorType =>
>         investorTypeCcyToTradingAccountMapByRegion(region)
>           .get((investorType, instrument.ccy))
>           .onNone(logger.error(s"No matching trading account for $investorType for instrument ${instrument.id} of ccy ${instrument.ccy}"))
>       }
>       .toList
>       .sorted(customTradingAccountTypeOrdering)
>   }
> ```
> 
> ‌
>

> 
> ```scala

> ```
> 
> ‌
> 
> Meanwhile in `SgFundSmartInstrumentBuilder`, we can resolve it according to customer
> 
> ```scala
>   protected def resolveBlacklistedInvestorTypes(maybeCustomerId: Option[UUID]): Future[Set[InvestorType]] = {
>     maybeCustomerId
>       .mapFut(customerService.getRegionalCustomer)
>       .map {
>         _.filter(RegionalCustomerDto.hasCpfSaAccount)
>           .map(_ => Set.empty[InvestorType])

>       }
>   }
> ```
> 
> ‌

## A1-2149 — At-least-once workflow approval uses stable requestIdSeed to dedupe investment

**Source stance:** explanation

**Context:**

> component: advisory-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/advisory/impl/productline/helpers/B2BProductHelpers.scala; operation: [INV-3426] feat(bff, workflowengine, advisory, goal, investment): Create subsequent investment for existing goal; trigger: Source-specific review condition as stated in the exact comment below.

**Concern stated in the source:** Full IdempotencyKey future; do not invest twice

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Idempotent means if same request is called twice \(or more\), we are able to de-dupe and execute it only once. Full fledge solution would involve properly implement `IdempotencyKey` , but for now, it should be sufficient if we rely on existing mechanism in `investment` svc to allow caller to set `investmentRequestId` via `requestIdSeed`
> 
> When a task is fully approved, workflow-engine will trigger this endpoint to perform the request \(sent in task payload\). The guarantee here is at-least-once. So we have to make sure we don’t invest multiple times if for whatever reason, it’s triggered multiple times by workflow-engine.

## A2-0182 — SgWorkflowEngineE4s: WorkflowEngineE4s

**Source stance:** explanation

**Context:**

> PR 10647 (Feat/AD-2007 b2b approvals bff), workflowengine-api/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/workflowengine/api/SgWorkflowEngineE4s.scala; original row 182.

**Concern stated in the source:** Current advisor/client portal split duplicates the pending-my-approval route until FE clients are unified.

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> WorkflowEngineE4s
> 
> ```
> /pending-approvals/creator/:creatorId?assigneeRole
> /pending-approvals/assignee/:assigneeId
> ```
> 
> ‌
> 
> BFF
> 
> ```
> A. my-created-and-pending-manager-requests/taskType/:taskType
> - calls /pending-approvals/creator/<authenticated-employeeId>?assigneeRole=FA_MANAGER
> - RBAC: Create action for RBAC resource coresponding to taskType
> 
> B. my-created-and-pending-client-requests/taskType/:taskType
> - calls /pending-approvals/creator/<authenticated-employeeId>?assigneeRole=CLIENT
> - RBAC: Create action for RBAC resource coresponding to taskType
> 
> C. pending-my-approval/taskType/:taskType
> - calls /pending-approvals/assignee/<authenticated-employeeId/customerId>
> - RBAC: Approve action for RBAC resource coresponding to taskType
> ```
> 
> ‌
> 
> BFF currently splits advisor-portal \(AdvisorPortal\*\) and client-portal \(SilverFe\*\). This means \(C\) needs to be duplicated.
> 
> BFF will eventually unify the FE clients \(every endpoint need to support all user types, as long as they pass the RBAC and guards validation\)

**Conditions and limits:**

- Keep the three concrete route/RBAC mappings from the source; pending-my-approval is duplicated until client unification.

## A2-0282 — PlanFeeInstructionEntity: The entity state is default with empty fee instructions, it means the plan always exists, just without any data. Modelling it this way means you can’t ...

**Source stance:** open-question

**Context:**

> PR 10030 ([EN-3952] (charge) Create new PlanFeeInstructionEntity), charge-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/charge/impl/entities/instruction/PlanFeeInstructionEntity.scala; original row 282.

**Concern stated in the source:** Empty default instructions cannot distinguish never-initialized from upserted-then-deleted plan state.

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> The entity state is default with empty fee instructions, it means the plan always exists, just without any data. Modelling it this way means you can’t distinguish between a uninitialized plan vs a plan with upserted-then-deleted fee instructions.
> 
> If we care enough about this, then we probably should make state a sealed trait, default with case object NotInitialized, otherwise it’s case class Initialized\(feeInstructions\). Then you can throw for GetCmd/DeleteCmd on NotInitialized. And no-op without error if deleting already deleted fee instruction for Initialized, and even throw if deleting last entry for Initialized \(to ensure there’s always an entry to support the fee rate query\)

**Conditions and limits:**

- The sealed NotInitialized/Initialized state is conditional on caring about that distinction; no-op deletion and last-entry rejection are proposals within that model.
- PR title and inline path identify source component/operation context only; quoted PR title is metadata, not a claim that the comment proposal was implemented.

## A2-0283 — PlanFeeInstructionEntity: Just thinking out loud, I’m not sure about capturing this effectiveEndDate in the event

**Source stance:** open-question

**Context:**

> PR 10030 ([EN-3952] (charge) Create new PlanFeeInstructionEntity), charge-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/charge/impl/entities/instruction/PlanFeeInstructionEntity.scala; original row 283.

**Concern stated in the source:** effectiveEndDate is derived, cannot be reconstructed at event-creation state by projection, and changing one instruction generally affects two instruction end dates.

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Just thinking out loud, I’m not sure about capturing this effectiveEndDate in the event
> 
> * It’s derived data, but I understand the concern that projection is not able to derive by itself since projection does not have access to the state at the point of event creation
> * It’s somewhat incomplete, because we would typically affect effectiveEndDate of 2 instructions, but we only emit for the one being upserted / deleted
> 
> If the intention is to provide ability for projection \(or even external topic subscriber\) to reconstruct the exact state, we can consider emit 2 events instead, one for the individual change, and one for the state \(pattern “Event-Carried State Transfer”\). This comes with its own pros & cons, but I think it’s cleaner and more flexible than stamping single effective end date here.
> 
> ‌
> 
> The field is logically optional right now. We can revisit this later if needed.

**Conditions and limits:**

- Two events (individual change plus state transfer) are an option with pros/cons; effectiveEndDate is currently logically optional and may be revisited.
- PR title and inline path identify source component/operation context only; quoted PR title is metadata, not a claim that the comment proposal was implemented.

```
// all APIs here will require Tenant from TracingContext

}

}
```

‌

Then BFF will essentially proxy `getInstrumentDetailsForFA` and `getInstrumentDetailsForClient` as authenticated endpoint \(I will make PR so that BFF will also set CustomerId in TracingContext, in addition to TenantId\), while `getInstrumentDetailsWithoutAuth` with be proxied using public endpoint.

‌

In `BaseAdvisoryServiceImpl`, we will lookup and call corresponding logic method

* `getInstrumentDetailsForFA` should call inner logic with AI/PI investorType and tenantId as corporate profile
* `getInstrumentDetailsForClient` should call inner logic with AI/PI or Retail investorType look up from customerId, and tenantId as corporate profile
* `getInstrumentDetailsWithoutAuth` should call inner logic with Retail investorType and none as corporate profile

And the inner logic would be reusable code

‌

## A2-0434 — Review: I think we should:

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 10262 (Feat/INV-3637 bff endpoint upload document), no inline path; original row 434.

**Concern stated in the source:** Document upload has no customer context, whereas GET must verify customer/context ownership in the domain edge service.

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> I think we should:
> 
> * create new endpoint in document svc `/api/v1/document/upload` with this UploadDocumentRequest type \(maybe optional documentId if there is need to control this id from caller\), and its logic calls `createDocumentWithBinaries` providing the OTHERS value for the deprecated enums
> * create authenticated endpoint in BFF proxy to above endpoint in document svc, for advisor portal, ~~which requires \(CUSTOMER:DOCUMENT resource & Create permission\)~~
> * do not allow for client portal for now, since there is no planned flow that requires this yet
> 
> ‌
> 
> Later on when we add GET endpoints, then it will be applicable for both advisor portal and client portal, ~~both require \(CUSTOMER:DOCUMENT resource & Read permission\)~~
> 
> Unlike the POST upload endpoint which doesn’t care about the context of document, the GET ones must care and validate the document indeed belongs to the customer \+ context. Hence these GET endpoints will have to be edge in the context service, e.g. goal/customer svc instead of direct document svc. This means these services would be responsible to capture the generated documentId from the upload endpoint.
> 
> ‌
> 
> Example for add goal flow:
> 
> * FA uploads document in advisor-portal → calls BFF to proxy to document svc → advisor-portal captures generated documentId
> * FA confirms to create the add-goal approval request in advisor-portal → calls BFF to proxy to advisory svc, which eventually creates workflow in workflow-engine
> 
>     * The workflow request must contain all the documentIds associated with this add-goal request
>     
> * When workflow request is fully approved → workflow-engine calls advisory svc which calls goal svc to create goal
> 
>     * We need to somehow persist these documentIds to the goalId
>     
> * When customer retrieves suitability doc from goal page in client-portal → calls BFF to proxy to goal svc `GET /api/v1/goal/:goalId/document` or `GET /api/v1/goal/:goalId/document/:documentId`
> 
>     * BFF validates goalId belongs to customerId
>     * goal svc validates documentId belongs to goalId
>     
> 
> ‌

**Conditions and limits:**

- The CUSTOMER:DOCUMENT RBAC suggestions in this source comment are struck through and clarified in row 436; do not revive them as requirements for bare upload.

Once it reaches the handler \(logic layer\), it is up to the domain to decide how they want to implement it. Example:

1. they could use an endpoint in BE that expects customerId in either payload or query param \(and hence we can simply reuse it completely, and define it as proxy endpoint in BFF\)
2. they could set context using CustomerProvider, and call the endpoint in BE that expects customerId from context instead \(and if not available, 500 error is rightfully thrown\)

I would prefer \(1\) instead and we stick to setting TenantId/CustomerId/EmployeeId context by auth only.

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> In on-behalf operations:
> 
> * auth user would be employee, which we would set into context using EmployeeProvider
> * and the request \(either payload or query param\) should specify the customer, which we would use to validate proper ownership/relationship in guards
> 
> ‌
> 
> Once it reaches the handler \(logic layer\), it is up to the domain to decide how they want to implement it. Example:
> 
> 1. they could use an endpoint in BE that expects customerId in either payload or query param \(and hence we can simply reuse it completely, and define it as proxy endpoint in BFF\)
> 2. they could set context using CustomerProvider, and call the endpoint in BE that expects customerId from context instead \(and if not available, 500 error is rightfully thrown\)
> 
> I would prefer \(1\) instead and we stick to setting TenantId/CustomerId/EmployeeId context by auth only.

## A2-0544 — HkChargeCommunicationProjection: This logic actually exists in `InitiateFeeRedemptionCmdHandler`, it’s best we rely on sequence of events, rather than duplicating it again.

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 10103 (Release/EN-3547 hk fee charge), charge-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/charge/impl/entities/manager/processors/hk/HkChargeCommunicationProjection.scala; original row 544.

**Concern stated in the source:** This logic actually exists in `InitiateFeeRedemptionCmdHandler`, it’s best we rely on sequence of events, rather than duplicating it again.

The communication logic in fact can be region agnostic as well \(the same way `InitiateFeeRedemptionCmdHandler` doesn’t care about sg or hk\). We can simply use the `redemptionDetails` \(instead of using amount from `discountDetails`, and having to assume that there is no tax involved\)

```
event.feeChargeRequest.redemptionDetails match {
  case Some(redemptionDetails) =>
    redemptionDetails.redeemedAmount match {
      case Some(chargeAmount) =>
        ...communication logic goes here...
      case None =>
        logger.error("... <unexpected-please-check> ... ")
        Future.successful(Done)
    }
  case None =>
    // waived without vouchers
    Future.successful(Done)
}
```

‌

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> This logic actually exists in `InitiateFeeRedemptionCmdHandler`, it’s best we rely on sequence of events, rather than duplicating it again.
> 
> The communication logic in fact can be region agnostic as well \(the same way `InitiateFeeRedemptionCmdHandler` doesn’t care about sg or hk\). We can simply use the `redemptionDetails` \(instead of using amount from `discountDetails`, and having to assume that there is no tax involved\)
> 
> ```
> event.feeChargeRequest.redemptionDetails match {
>   case Some(redemptionDetails) =>
>     redemptionDetails.redeemedAmount match {
>       case Some(chargeAmount) =>
>         ...communication logic goes here...
>       case None =>
>         logger.error("... <unexpected-please-check> ... ")
>         Future.successful(Done)
>     }
>   case None =>
>     // waived without vouchers
>     Future.successful(Done)
> }
> ```
> 
> ‌

**Conditions and limits:**

- Communication follows FeeChargeCompletedEvt redemptionDetails: Some redeemedAmount sends; missing redeemedAmount logs unexpected and returns Done; None redemptionDetails is waived without vouchers and returns Done.

**Concern stated in the source:** If this cmd handler does not support B2B types, let match and reject it outside, then pass in only the resolved B2C type

```
def handleUpdateProductCharacteristicsCmd(cmd: UpdateProductCharacteristicsCmd, state: GoalState): Reply = {
  cmd.newProductLineAndIntent match {
      case x: productline.B2CProductLineAndIntent =>
        handleUpdateB2CProductCharacteristicsCmd(cmd, state, x)
      case _: productline.B2BProductLineAndIntent =>
        Effect.reply(cmd.replyTo)(
          GoalSvcException("Invalid product line and intent, only supports B2C product lines", GoalSvcErrorType.???).error
        )
  }
} 
```

‌

If this cmd handler can be generic, then we simply don’t emit the B2C events instead of throwing

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

>       case _: productline.B2BProductLineAndIntent =>

>         )
>   }
> } 
> ```
>

## A2-0597 — ModelPortfolioEntity: So there are 2 events:

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 10034 (Resolve INV-3485: Changes to wait for response in subscriber, react to PortfolioAllocationTargetUpdatedMsg in rebalance.), portfolio-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/portfolio/impl/entities/portfolio/ModelPortfolioEntity.scala; original row 597.

**Concern stated in the source:** So there are 2 events:

* `PortfolioMovedToNewAllocationTargetEvt` is purely for TAA change. You can see `handleUpdateCurrentAllocationTargetCmd` \(the real cmd handler for emitting this evt\) only checks `effectiveDate` and `List[AllocationTarget]`
* `PortfolioAllocationTargetUpdatedEvt` is intended to update underlying instrument profile \(of the `AllocationTarget`\). We don’t really need this evt for the clone purpose. And even if needed, it should come via the instrument cloning instead.

‌

Advisory’s ProductPortfolio handles both PortfolioMovedToNewAllocationTargetMsg and PortfolioAllocationTargetUpdatedMsg. I don’t remember if we have migrated everything to refresh instrument data always, but this entity has a rework as we discussed in the past \(it just needs to store the tagging, and fetch fresh or projection portfolio/instrument data\). I think until then, let’s just leave it.

‌

> * `PortfolioAllocationTargetUpdatedEvt` is intended to update underlying instrument profile \(of the `AllocationTarget`\). We don’t really need this evt for the clone purpose. And even if needed, it should come via the instrument cloning instead.

## A2-0718 — PortfolioMonthlyChangesHelper: I think there are 2 types of race conditions we might see here:

**Source stance:** observed-defect

**Context:**

> PR 9603 (Feat/INV-3271 marketdata portfolio entity phase 1), marketdata-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/marketdata/impl/helpers/PortfolioMonthlyChangesHelper.scala; original row 718.

**Concern stated in the source:** I think there are 2 types of race conditions we might see here:

1. We get event that instrument mc is updated, and we trigger this method which will query instrument mc from readside - that might not have latest data yet… cuz they are 2 independent projections

    * We override the data for the instrument being updated, but it’s not bullet proof, e.g. db projection is super lagged for some reason
    
        * event of instrumentA, its data A2 is overridden on top of existing readside A1 & B1
        * then event of instrumentB, its data B2 is overridden on top of stale A1 & B1
        
    
2. Multiple instruments might be updated at once, each of them triggering this method… their upsert might override each other

    * This was protected with Portfolio entity last time. So we might need some impl of optimistic locking here
    

‌

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> I think there are 2 types of race conditions we might see here:
> 
> 1. We get event that instrument mc is updated, and we trigger this method which will query instrument mc from readside - that might not have latest data yet… cuz they are 2 independent projections
> 
>     * We override the data for the instrument being updated, but it’s not bullet proof, e.g. db projection is super lagged for some reason
>     
>         * event of instrumentA, its data A2 is overridden on top of existing readside A1 & B1
>         * then event of instrumentB, its data B2 is overridden on top of stale A1 & B1
>         
>     
> 2. Multiple instruments might be updated at once, each of them triggering this method… their upsert might override each other
> 
>     * This was protected with Portfolio entity last time. So we might need some impl of optimistic locking here
>     
> 
> ‌

**Conditions and limits:**

- Two separate races remain: independent projection lag can pair new B2 with stale A1 despite per-event override, and concurrent instrument-triggered portfolio upserts can overwrite each other. Optimistic locking is proposed as entity replacement protection.
- PR title and inline path identify source component/operation context only; quoted PR title is metadata, not a claim that the comment proposal was implemented.

## A2-0783 — SgRecommendedInvestmentManager: Best if we can refactor to avoid make unnecessary calls

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 9739 (Feat/EN-3683 sg create a new api to get recommended investment amount), advisory-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/advisory/impl/managers/sg/SgRecommendedInvestmentManager.scala; original row 783.

**Concern stated in the source:** Best if we can refactor to avoid make unnecessary calls

```
lazy val tierLevelFut = getCustomerIncomeTierLevel(customerId)
lazy val myInfoFinancialDataFut = getMyInfoFinancialData(customerId)

tradingAccountType match {
  case TradingAccountType.SINGAPORE_SGD_CASH_ACCOUNT =>
    tierLevelFut.map { level =>
      deriveRecommendationFromIncomeTier(level, RecommendedRecurringMonthlyAmountSgdCashBasedOnIncomeLevelMap)
    }

  case TradingAccountType.SINGAPORE_CPF_OA_ACCOUNT =>
    for {
      myInfoFinancialData <- myInfoFinancialDataFut
      response <- deriveRecommendationFromMyInfo(myInfoFinancialData) match {
        case Some(recommendation) =>
          Future.successful(recommendation)
        case None =>
          tierLevelFut.map { level =>
            deriveRecommendationFromIncomeTier(level, RecommendedRecurringMonthlyAmountCpfBasedOnIncomeLevelMap)
          }
      }
    } yield response

  case _ =>
    Future.successful(RecommendedInvestmentDto.noRecommendation())
}
```

‌

No need to split the helper methods too fine, especially when they are not used in more than one place

* `getCustomerIncomeTierLevel` can do both customer lookup and perform mapping to TierLevel
* `getMyInfoFinancialData` can do myinfo lookup, if found then return, else only then do onboarding lookup and perform mapping

‌

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Best if we can refactor to avoid make unnecessary calls
> 
> ```
> lazy val tierLevelFut = getCustomerIncomeTierLevel(customerId)
> lazy val myInfoFinancialDataFut = getMyInfoFinancialData(customerId)
> 
> tradingAccountType match {
>   case TradingAccountType.SINGAPORE_SGD_CASH_ACCOUNT =>
>     tierLevelFut.map { level =>
>       deriveRecommendationFromIncomeTier(level, RecommendedRecurringMonthlyAmountSgdCashBasedOnIncomeLevelMap)
>     }
> 
>   case TradingAccountType.SINGAPORE_CPF_OA_ACCOUNT =>
>     for {
>       myInfoFinancialData <- myInfoFinancialDataFut
>       response <- deriveRecommendationFromMyInfo(myInfoFinancialData) match {
>         case Some(recommendation) =>
>           Future.successful(recommendation)
>         case None =>
>           tierLevelFut.map { level =>
>             deriveRecommendationFromIncomeTier(level, RecommendedRecurringMonthlyAmountCpfBasedOnIncomeLevelMap)
>           }
>       }
>     } yield response
> 
>   case _ =>
>     Future.successful(RecommendedInvestmentDto.noRecommendation())
> }
> ```
> 
> ‌
> 
> No need to split the helper methods too fine, especially when they are not used in more than one place
> 
> * `getCustomerIncomeTierLevel` can do both customer lookup and perform mapping to TierLevel
> * `getMyInfoFinancialData` can do myinfo lookup, if found then return, else only then do onboarding lookup and perform mapping
> 
> ‌

**Conditions and limits:**

- SGD uses only income-tier lookup; CPF tries MyInfo first, falling back to income tier only if needed; unsupported account returns noRecommendation. Customer/onboarding lookup should also be lazy.

## A2-0821 — ProductPortfolioRepository: Maybe we can keep this method generic, but only handle for CoreEnhanced for now…

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 9605 ([INV-3236] feat(advisory): create advisory endpoints for goal create), advisory-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/advisory/impl/entities/portfolio/db/repository/ProductPortfolioRepository.scala; original row 821.

**Concern stated in the source:** Maybe we can keep this method generic, but only handle for CoreEnhanced for now…

```
def findProductPortfolio(
  advisoryTag: AdvisoryTag,
  riskTarget: ModelPortfolioRiskTarget,
  tradingAccountType: TradingAccountType
): Future[ProductPortfolio] = {
  findAllActiveForAdvisoryTag(advisoryTag)
    .filter(p => filterForTradingAccountType(advisoryTag, tradingAccountType, p))
    .filter(p => filterForRiskTarget(advisoryTag, riskTarget, p))
    .runWith(Sink.headOption)
    .flatMap({
      case Some(productPortfolio) => Future.successful(productPortfolio)
      case None =>
        Future
          .failed(BadRequest(s"Unable to find $advisoryTag portfolio for trading account $tradingAccountType with risk target of $riskTarget"))
    })
}

private def filterForRiskTarget(advisoryTag: AdvisoryTag, riskTarget: ModelPortfolioRiskTarget, p: ProductPortfolio): Boolean = {
  advisoryTag match {
    case AdvisoryTag.CORE_ENHANCED =>
      ProductPortfolio.extractCoreEnhancedMetaData(p).exists(_.riskTarget == riskTarget)
    case _ => false
  }
}
```

‌

I want to keep the method signature as close to the lookup by targetStockRatio one so it’s easier to switch later for Flagship/Esg/Factors/FlagshipDpm

## A2-0861 — NonAltsFeeManager: We want the opposite. Honour the validated input flag always. Validation means these 2 checks

**Source stance:** suggestion

```

  throw BadRequest(s"CashOnlyFee is not supported for non-cash trading account: ${planProfile.tradingAccountType}")
}
```

and

```
isCashOnlyFeeRequired <- isCashOnlyFeeRequired(planId, planProfile.tradingAccountType)(isSellBlockedPlan)
_ = if (isCashOnlyFeeRequired && !request.cashOnlyFee.contains(true)) {
  throw BadRequest(s"CashOnlyFee is required for plan: $planId")
}
```

‌

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> We want the opposite. Honour the validated input flag always. Validation means these 2 checks
> 
> ```
> _ = if (request.cashOnlyFee.contains(true) && !TradingAccountType.isCash(planProfile.tradingAccountType)) {
>   throw BadRequest(s"CashOnlyFee is not supported for non-cash trading account: ${planProfile.tradingAccountType}")
> }
> ```
> 
> and
> 
> ```
> isCashOnlyFeeRequired <- isCashOnlyFeeRequired(planId, planProfile.tradingAccountType)(isSellBlockedPlan)
> _ = if (isCashOnlyFeeRequired && !request.cashOnlyFee.contains(true)) {
>   throw BadRequest(s"CashOnlyFee is required for plan: $planId")
> }
> ```
> 
> ‌

**Concern stated in the source:** Ok this one is not safe. On redemption trade side, cash reservations \(if any\) correspond to each individual orders, however if full redemption fee charge is involved, they will be merged and split to fund the fee amount.

Examples:

```
Normal redemption of 600 from 3 orders
{
  "settlementConfirmation": {
    "cashReservations": [100, 200, 300]
  },
  "cashReservations": [100, 200, 300]
}

Full redemption of 600 from 3 orders, with charge 10
{
  "settlementConfirmation": {
    "cashReservations": [100, 200, 300]
  },
  "cashReservations": [590]
}
```

‌

Amendment comes for full redemption comes, outer `cashReservations` needs to be updated/resplit from the settlement cash reservations

```
Full redemption of 600 -> 650 from 3 orders, with charge 10
{
  "settlementConfirmation": {
    "cashReservations": [100 -> 150, 200, 300]
  },
  "cashReservations": [640]
}
```

## A2-1059 — PageDataGenerator: Actually we have too many region pattern matching in this method. Maybe consolidate it a bit

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 9052 ([INV-3010] : update monthly statement to include dpm section), report-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/report/impl/statement/data/statementDataGenerator/goalBasedStatement/PageDataGenerator.scala; original row 1059.

**Concern stated in the source:** Actually we have too many region pattern matching in this method. Maybe consolidate it a bit

```
def headTailMapper(...)

def generate(goals: List[GoalRowDetails], isDPM: Boolean, maxRowsInFirstPage: Int, firstPageTemplate: String, subsequentPageTemplate: String): List[(AllInvestmentGoalsPageData, String)] = ...

region match {
  case SilverRegion.Sg =>
    // SG AllInvestmentGoals templates do not distinguish DPM and non-DPM goals, hence treating all goals as non-DPM
    generate(
      goals = pageData.goalDetails.asScala.toList,
      isDPM = false,
      maxRowsInFirstPage = maxRowsPerAllInvestmentsPage,
      firstPageTemplate = "allInvestmentGoalsPage",
      subsequentPageTemplate = "allInvestmentGoalsPureGoalsPage"
    )
  case SilverRegion.Hk =>
    // HK AllInvestmentGoals templates have special empty page
    if (pageData.goalDetails.isEmpty) {
      List((pageData.copy(goalDetails = pageData.goalDetails), "allInvestmentGoalsPageWithoutGoal"))
    } else {
      val allInvestmentDPMPageData = generate(
        goals = pageData.goalDetails.asScala.toList.filter(_.isDiscretionary),
        isDPM = true,
        maxRowsInFirstPage = maxRowsPerAllInvestmentsPageForFirstDPMPage,
        firstPageTemplate = "allInvestmentGoalsPage",
        subsequentPageTemplate = "allInvestmentGoalsPureGoalsPage"
      )
      val allInvestmentNonDPMPageData = generate(
        goals = pageData.goalDetails.asScala.toList.filterNot(_.isDiscretionary),
        isDPM = false,
        maxRowsInFirstPage = maxRowsPerAllInvestmentsPage,
        firstPageTemplate = "allInvestmentNonDPMGoalsPage",
        subsequentPageTemplate = "allInvestmentGoalsPureGoalsPage"
      )
      allInvestmentDPMPageData ++ allInvestmentNonDPMPageData
    }
  case _ => throw new Exception(s"AllInvestmentGoalsPageData generator behaviour not configured for region $region.")
}
```

‌

## A2-1081 — ReportApplication: Just some notes here, yall are right about the trade-offs but manual start is not that bad, depending on use cases.

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 9306 (Feat/EN-3405 use tasktopicsubscriber in report for manual start/stop), report-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/report/impl/ReportApplication.scala; original row 1081.

**Concern stated in the source:** Just some notes here, yall are right about the trade-offs but manual start is not that bad, depending on use cases.

In case of report, the svc itself is responsible for triggering of the topic producer side. So we can potentially just call start \(via distributed pubsub\) in the same trigger endpoint, i.e. `createMonthlyStatementsV2` first will trigger start, only then produce the message.

* the start is idempotent so if already started, it won’t cause any harm
* the distributed pubsub is at-most once tho, so it could still happen that maybe one of instance does not start… but I suppose this could be checked easily via logs or metrics.

‌

We can also make this pause/resume status persisted, and check upon startup :thumbsup: 

‌

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Just some notes here, yall are right about the trade-offs but manual start is not that bad, depending on use cases.
> 
> In case of report, the svc itself is responsible for triggering of the topic producer side. So we can potentially just call start \(via distributed pubsub\) in the same trigger endpoint, i.e. `createMonthlyStatementsV2` first will trigger start, only then produce the message.
> 
> * the start is idempotent so if already started, it won’t cause any harm
> * the distributed pubsub is at-most once tho, so it could still happen that maybe one of instance does not start… but I suppose this could be checked easily via logs or metrics.
> 
> ‌
> 
> We can also make this pause/resume status persisted, and check upon startup :thumbsup: 
> 
> ‌

**Conditions and limits:**

- Report may start TaskTopicSubscriber idempotently before producing in createMonthlyStatementsV2. Distributed pubsub is at-most-once and may miss an instance; logs/metrics can detect it. Persisted pause/resume is another option.
- PR title and inline path identify source component/operation context only; quoted PR title is metadata, not a claim that the comment proposal was implemented.

## A2-1083 — Review: Trading team will:

**Source stance:** explanation

**Context:**

> PR 9296 ([INV-3070] revert(advisory): revert fx supported ccy validation in advisory endpoint), no inline path; original row 1083.

**Concern stated in the source:** Trading team will:

* add supported ccy validation for indicative quote
* after cash reservation is accepted, this is validated again before we make the actual fx conversion - if error, will block the trade. TradeOps then can intervene as usual, i.e. delete/cancel the trade

‌

The above scenario can happen even if we add this validation in advisory. Example: ccy X is supported on T, we allow goal creation…. T\+1 something is wrong, and we remove support for that ccy… T\+2 investment is funded, and fxconversion will now fail

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Trading team will:
> 
> * add supported ccy validation for indicative quote
> * after cash reservation is accepted, this is validated again before we make the actual fx conversion - if error, will block the trade. TradeOps then can intervene as usual, i.e. delete/cancel the trade
> 
> ‌
> 
> The above scenario can happen even if we add this validation in advisory. Example: ccy X is supported on T, we allow goal creation…. T\+1 something is wrong, and we remove support for that ccy… T\+2 investment is funded, and fxconversion will now fail

**Conditions and limits:**

- Supported FX currencies may change between goal creation T, removal T+1 and funding T+2; advisory-time validation cannot prevent this. Revalidate before actual conversion, block trade on failure, and TradeOps can cancel/delete.
- PR title and inline path identify source component/operation context only; quoted PR title is metadata, not a claim that the comment proposal was implemented.
- No inline hunk is available in the source row; the comment does not identify any omitted symbol more precisely.

**Concern stated in the source:** Oh we definitely want to set `rejectionHandler` for all services, especially when we extract this to common code. And in order to use a custom rejection handler, we need to use `Route.seal` with implicit `rejectionHandler`

I took a shortcut and only added for the services we need back then \(some issue in FE sending incorrect payload, and we reject with validation errors not in json, and Davinci doesn’t log full error msg\)

## A2-1239 — DetectExpiredInvestmentRequestProcessor: [person] [person] [person] Is the below correct understanding?

**Source stance:** open-question

**Context:**

> PR 8955 (TT-4210 investment request expiry detection skip for auto funding), investment-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/investment/impl/schedulers/DetectExpiredInvestmentRequestProcessor.scala; original row 1239.

**Concern stated in the source:** [person] [person] [person] Is the below correct understanding?

* autofx: If `fxConversionRequestId` is available here, it means cash is reserved for fx conversion, and we will ensure the conversion will happen. Hence, we will not expire the investment, regardless of `isRequestExpired`. If for whatever reason, the conversion cannot happen,  investment is cancelled elsewhere \(with adequate alerts if needs to manually cancel\).
* autofund: if `autoFundInstruction` is available here, we will ensure the deposit will happen. If there are failures, retry logic will consider expiry \+ cutOff into retry date. Hence, we will not expire the investment, regardless of `isRequestExpired`. And similarly, if for whatever reason, the deposit cannot happen,  investment is cancelled elsewhere \(with adequate alerts if needs to manually cancel\).

‌

If correct, can you please help to add this explanation here, so that it’s easy to understand this logic in future :pray: 

‌

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> [person] [person] [person] Is the below correct understanding?
> 
> * autofx: If `fxConversionRequestId` is available here, it means cash is reserved for fx conversion, and we will ensure the conversion will happen. Hence, we will not expire the investment, regardless of `isRequestExpired`. If for whatever reason, the conversion cannot happen,  investment is cancelled elsewhere \(with adequate alerts if needs to manually cancel\).
> * autofund: if `autoFundInstruction` is available here, we will ensure the deposit will happen. If there are failures, retry logic will consider expiry \+ cutOff into retry date. **Concern stated in the source:** We can extract amount validation into a method

```
  def validateAmountRestriction(maybeAmount: Option[BigDecimal], maybeRestriction: Option[SubscriptionAmountRegulation], context: String): Future[Done] = {
    maybeRestriction match {
      case Some(restriction) =>
        val expectedAmount = adjustAmount(maybeAmount, restriction)
        if (maybeAmount != expectedAmount) {
          Future.failed(BadRequest(s"$context breaches amount restrictions: request $maybeAmount, expected $expectedAmount"))
        } else {
          Future.successful(Done)
        }
      case None =>
        Future.successful(Done)
    }
  }
```

‌

And let caller decide how to extract amount \+ restriction, then handle Option themselves.

We can additionally create another method to extract amount for `PlanInvestmentBasedRequest` or `PlanUpsertInvestmentBasedRequest` if needed

## A2-1308 — Review: In Invest, for new tables \+ projection, we typically include version in the name of the classes, so that there are clean code changes in the PR: 1st PR to add new versi...

**Source stance:** explanation

**Context:**

> PR 8961 ([EN-3099] feat(goal): Migrate to use new goal tables), no inline path; original row 1308.

**Concern stated in the source:** In Invest, for new tables \+ projection, we typically include version in the name of the classes, so that there are clean code changes in the PR: 1st PR to add new version, and 2nd PR to remove old version \(without touching new ones anymore\)

Goal svc has not been migrated with this yet, hence you don’t see same pattern. But here this PR would be half the size if we just remove the old version

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> In Invest, for new tables \+ projection, we typically include version in the name of the classes, so that there are clean code changes in the PR: 1st PR to add new version, and 2nd PR to remove old version \(without touching new ones anymore\)
> 
> Goal svc has not been migrated with this yet, hence you don’t see same pattern. But here this PR would be half the size if we just remove the old version

**Conditions and limits:**

- Historical Invest convention uses explicit versioned table/projection classes: add new in first PR, remove old in second without touching new. This is a migration review convention, not universal naming law.
- PR title and inline path identify source component/operation context only; quoted PR title is metadata, not a claim that the comment proposal was implemented.
- No inline hunk is available in the source row; the comment does not identify any omitted symbol more precisely.

> 
> ‌

Source(instrument)

      .map(_ => Right(Done))

      }

```

* new instance: convert V2 to V3 request, create cmd with both amount and fundingInstructions

* new instance: create plan with both amount and fundingInstructions \(new behaviour\)

## A2-1585 — TransactionTypes: We can let the old `FxConversionDetails` having optional accounts, as we are migrating away from this v1 model.

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 8011 (TT-3566 Make broker account optional for FX transactions), transaction-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/transaction/impl/common/TransactionTypes.scala; original row 1585.

**Concern stated in the source:** We can let the old `FxConversionDetails` having optional accounts, as we are migrating away from this v1 model.

For new `FxTransaction` model:

* Changing `debitBrokerAccount` and `creditBrokerAccount` to optional here makes sense. All existing fx conversion txn would have them populated, and hence still compatible with old FE.
* But I think it’s also good to capture the fact that broker accounts will be available when the txn is settled. Maybe we can consider the following:

    * Add new `SettledFxStatusDetailsV2` that is identical with `SettledFxStatusDetails` with additionally the 2 required broker account fields
    * Change kafka subscriber to populate transaction using V2 instead of V1
    * Add 2 required broker account fields into `SettledFxStatusDetailsDto`
    
        * If entity has V2, map as is
        * If entity has V1, require the outer optional broker account fields in `FxTransaction` to be defined
        
    

‌

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> We can let the old `FxConversionDetails` having optional accounts, as we are migrating away from this v1 model.
> 
> For new `FxTransaction` model:
> 
> * Changing `debitBrokerAccount` and `creditBrokerAccount` to optional here makes sense. All existing fx conversion txn would have them populated, and hence still compatible with old FE.
> * But I think it’s also good to capture the fact that broker accounts will be available when the txn is settled. Maybe we can consider the following:
> 
>     * Add new `SettledFxStatusDetailsV2` that is identical with `SettledFxStatusDetails` with additionally the 2 required broker account fields
>     * Change kafka subscriber to populate transaction using V2 instead of V1
>     * Add 2 required broker account fields into `SettledFxStatusDetailsDto`
>     
>         * If entity has V2, map as is
>         * If entity has V1, require the outer optional broker account fields in `FxTransaction` to be defined
>         
>     
> 
> ‌

**Conditions and limits:**

- Old FxConversionDetails can retain optional accounts while new settled FX V2 status requires accounts; V1 DTO conversion must require populated outer accounts.

## A2-1620 — RebateDistributionCommunicationsManager: Each customer wouldn’t have too many trailer rebates per quarter, so I suppose it’s ok to run this aggregation in memory. But we potenti...

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 8353 (Feat/INV-1996/automate trailer rebate), rebate-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/rebate/impl/logic/managers/RebateDistributionCommunicationsManager.scala; original row 1620.

**Concern stated in the source:** Each customer wouldn’t have too many trailer rebates per quarter, so I suppose it’s ok to run this aggregation in memory. But we potentially can push this down to database query and it would be more memory efficient \+ faster computation there.

Example in BQ. Then we can enrich the instrument \+ mandatory rebate data bits on the fly

```
SELECT
  r.customerId,
  r.broker,
  SUM(r.distributedRebateAmount),
  ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT r.instrumentId)
FROM
  silver_raw_dataset.rebate_distribution_requests r
WHERE
  r.fromDate >= '2023-07-01'
  AND r.toDate <= '2023-09-30'
GROUP BY
  r.customerId,
  r.broker
ORDER BY
  r.customerId,
  r.broker
```

‌

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Each customer wouldn’t have too many trailer rebates per quarter, so I suppose it’s ok to run this aggregation in memory. But we potentially can push this down to database query and it would be more memory efficient \+ faster computation there.
> 
> Example in BQ. Then we can enrich the instrument \+ mandatory rebate data bits on the fly
> 
> ```
> SELECT
>   r.customerId,
>   r.broker,
>   SUM(r.distributedRebateAmount),
>   ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT r.instrumentId)
> FROM
>   silver_raw_dataset.rebate_distribution_requests r
> WHERE
>   r.fromDate >= '2023-07-01'
>   AND r.toDate <= '2023-09-30'
> GROUP BY
>   r.customerId,
>   r.broker
> ORDER BY
>   r.customerId,
>   r.broker
> ```
> 
> ‌

**Conditions and limits:**

- Per-customer quarterly data is small enough for in-memory aggregation, but database grouping customerId/broker, SUM(distributedRebateAmount), ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT instrumentId) and later streaming enrichment is an optimization proposal.
- PR title and inline path identify source component/operation context only; quoted PR title is metadata, not a claim that the comment proposal was implemented.

## A2-1715 — AuroraJdbcSchema: Ah yes, creating them as empty is ok. My previous comment was in context of either the repository or the dbHandler having injected database.

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 7899 (PLATFORM-1097: Rebalance service pg readside migration), rebalance-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/rebalance/impl/db/AuroraJdbcSchema.scala; original row 1715.

**Concern stated in the source:** Ah yes, creating them as empty is ok. My previous comment was in context of either the repository or the dbHandler having injected database.

‌

Good examples:

```
_ <- database.run(someDbHandlerOrRepositoryInstanceWithoutInjectedDatabase.createTable)
_ <- database.run(SomeDbHandlerOrRepositoryCompanionObject.createTable)
```

In these cases, the Schema class with its injected database will decide where to create these tables. Hence we will create them in correct place \(even tho non-read-side ones will be empty cuz we haven’t migrated\)

‌

Potentially confusing example \(previous version of this PR\):

```
_ <- someDbHandlerOrRepositoryInstanceWithInjectedDatabase.createTable
```

Here, the injected database of Schema is ignored, and the dbHandler/repository will use its own injected database. And in this specific case, `rpcCommunicationDetailsJdbcRepository` and `planMarketValueJdbcHandler` both have only 1 instance using GCP jdbcDatabase.

‌

Either way, current PR looks good to me!

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Ah yes, creating them as empty is ok. My previous comment was in context of either the repository or the dbHandler having injected database.
> 
> ‌
> 
> Good examples:
> 
> ```
> _ <- database.run(someDbHandlerOrRepositoryInstanceWithoutInjectedDatabase.createTable)
> _ <- database.run(SomeDbHandlerOrRepositoryCompanionObject.createTable)
> ```
> 
> In these cases, the Schema class with its injected database will decide where to create these tables. Hence we will create them in correct place \(even tho non-read-side ones will be empty cuz we haven’t migrated\)
> 
> ‌
> 
> Potentially confusing example \(previous version of this PR\):
> 
> ```
> _ <- someDbHandlerOrRepositoryInstanceWithInjectedDatabase.createTable
> ```
> 
> Here, the injected database of Schema is ignored, and the dbHandler/repository will use its own injected database. And in this specific case, `rpcCommunicationDetailsJdbcRepository` and `planMarketValueJdbcHandler` both have only 1 instance using GCP jdbcDatabase.
> 
> ‌
> 
> Either way, current PR looks good to me!

**Conditions and limits:**

- The database controlling createTable matters: Schema.database.run(action) creates in chosen schema DB even if tables are empty, whereas child.createTable with injected DB silently targets child GCP. Current PR is accepted after that clarification.
- PR title and inline path identify source component/operation context only; quoted PR title is metadata, not a claim that the comment proposal was implemented.

## A3-0683 — StatusFields V1 bridge differs from always-present AssetTransfer units

**Source stance:** explanation

**Context:**

> transaction-api/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/transaction/api/models/TransactionTypes.scala; PR: [INV-1437] feat(transaction): Models

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> My rationale on not-using-StatusFields for this is:
> 
> * StatusFields is a bridge to V1 to support these optional-per-status fields, e.g. requestedAmount is None and only populated when transaction is created, settledAmount is None and only populated when transaction is settled etc
> * These fields are at top level in v1 TransactionDto, so the v2 to v1 mapping, we just blindly set them
> * Whereas in this AssetTransfer case, the field is required in v1 \(since we create dedicated v1 DTO for it\), and the value is always populated either with requestedUnits or settledUnits. This means `statusFields.requestedUnits` wouldn’t be used anywhere, but when it’s used for AssetTransfer, we will call `Option.get`. This is why it looks off in my head.

>     4. We can use same subscriber \(same consumer group\) to help with migration later. If different consumer group, we would need to double-release, one to turn off the old subscriber with logic, follow ed by another release to include logic in new subscriber.

## A3-0822 — Recurring failure email: actual reason, event-domain coupling and direct-publish deferral

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> investment-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/investment/impl/utils/communication/hk/HkRecurringInvestmentFailureEmailComposer.scala; PR: Resolve INV-1135: Send email for failed recurring investments with state change info

**Concern stated in the source:** And if we add all applicable compliance block reasons \(so that we can evolve the email logic freely\), we would also bake the compliance domain to investment event domain.

* Since it might fail, we should retry, and add support to retry manually via endpoint, if needed
* You can add all the failure reasons here, but no need to think too hard, cuz it’s all on the fly - nothing is persisted
* If it gets too slow and starts impacting the main triggering flow, we can revisit moving to event processor \(or postpone further by dispatching to another kafka topic, and construct the email and publish to communication from there\)

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Yeah simulation only makes sense if we want to warn user about potential failure in the upcoming-recurring-investment email. For this jira, we want to include exactly the failure reason. This means the entry point to construct the email should already contain the failure reason, passed from the `RecurringInvestmentProcessor`.
> 
> 
> 
> This can be achieved via Cmd\+Evt like what you did here. However, I feel we might couple our event domain with the copy \(suitability VS risk breach\), e.g today we add CrBreach as reason, tmr copy wants to distinguish between Cat1 breach vs Cat2 breach. And if we add all applicable compliance block reasons \(so that we can evolve the email logic freely\), we would also bake the compliance domain to investment event domain. Not to mention, we would likely support this to SG too - in which case, do we want to handle SG vs HK failure reason in the event?
> 
> 
> 
> The above is not necessarily wrong, but I don’t think we know everything to decide it now. And there’s a way to postpone this decision: by publishing directly to communication in the `RecurringInvestmentProcessor`
> 
> * Since it might fail, we should retry, and add support to retry manually via endpoint, if needed
> * You can add all the failure reasons here, but no need to think too hard, cuz it’s all on the fly - nothing is persisted
> * If it gets too slow and starts impacting the main triggering flow, we can revisit moving to event processor \(or postpone further by dispatching to another kafka topic, and construct the email and publish to communication from there\)
> 
> 
> 
> `RecurringInvestmentRequestFailedEvent` with proper region-specific failure reason sounds like a good thing to me, I’m just not sure we’re ready to implement it yet.

**Conditions and limits:**

- Source wording is preserved in requested_change; interrogatives and proposals are not settled answers.
- The component path and PR title identify source context only; merged/resolved status is not evidence of implementation or correctness.
- Keep upcoming-warning simulation distinct from actual failure reason. Persisted region/compliance/copy coupling is unresolved; direct publish with bounded retry/manual endpoint is a deferral option, later task topic/event flow conditional on slowness.

> OTOH, most of the time it’s harmless to leave the ack there. We can build recon logic for ack too, e.g. CAT1 goals with persisted CAT2 ack, goals with recurring investment with persisted recurring ack. This way, we can eventually fix the acks without building complicated workflow logic. And it’s ok because this only affects recurring flow, unlike earmark which will affect CR calculation.
> 
> I can update the logging message here a bit to indicate that we will have recon for it, instead of just purely “can ignore”.

## A3-1247 — Supplied TAA+ack sufficient for request; customer CR must honor TaaModificationEarmark

**Source stance:** explanation

**Context:**

> compliance-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/compliance/impl/logic/hk/service/TradingRestrictionLogic.scala; PR: Feat/INV-560 cra2 complex ack

**Concern stated in the source:** We don’t need to look up again, even in rare race condition in which exists a TaaModificationEarmark for same plan.

This is because it can happen to another completely different plan, as CR breach is validation at customer level.

Conclusion, we don’t need to change anything here, except for maybe find a way to structure/comment code so that this logic is clear for reader.

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> FYI…
> 
> I and  chatted offline on this topic:
> 
> * The request provides the TAA together with corresponding acks for that specific TAA. We don’t need to look up again, even in rare race condition in which exists a TaaModificationEarmark for same plan. If such case happens:
> 
>     * goal modification request itself should already ack for its corresponding new TAA. So either one of the goal modification or investment request will have correct ack
>     * investment orders will anyhow be generated much later by trading service - potentially using a different TAA at that time. As long as we guarantee all trading impact activities go thru latest ack check, it’s sufficient
>     
> * OTOH, CR calculation should lookup TAA honouring TaaModificationEarmark. This is because it can happen to another completely different plan, as CR breach is validation at customer level.
> 
> 
> 
> Conclusion, we don’t need to change anything here, except for maybe find a way to structure/comment code so that this logic is clear for reader. But we can revisit refactoring after we capture the essential logic \+ extensive test cases.

**Conditions and limits:**

- Source wording is preserved in requested_change; interrogatives and proposals are not settled answers.
- The component path and PR title identify source context only; merged/resolved status is not evidence of implementation or correctness.
- The hunk evidence is source context; symbols or conditions found only there must not be attributed to the comment.
- Final source decision distinguishes request-supplied TAA+corresponding ack for goal/investment from customer-levelCR requiring TaaModificationEarmark lookup; no change here beyond comments/refactor after tests.
- Related source rows 3124, 3126, 3127: Earmark-aware lookup proposal is revised: request-supplied TAA+ack here; customer-levelCR honors earmark.

## R-3538 — Final optional event fields defer optional-forever versus mandatory-plus-migration choice

**Source stance:** requested-change

**Context:**

> dividend-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/dividend/impl/entities/dividend/ces/DividendEvents.scala; PR 2833: SILVER-11229: Fix settlement date for dividend reinvestment

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> All new fields are now optional in events, hence all JsonMigration steps are removed.
> 
> We can:
> 
> A. Keep them optional forever to correctly reflect the event history, i.e. they are indeed new fields that were added at some point of time.
> 
> B. Make them mandatory \+ add back the migration step to provide default value in separate release
> 
> ‌
> 
> \(A\) would force new event processors to think and handle them, since all events will be re-processed by them. They might fallback to default values, or not. \(A\) give them an obligation to handle, but a choice to choose.
> 
> \(B\) effectively forces all new event processors to follow the default value via the serializer.
> 
> ‌
> 
> Making them optional now defer the decision of choosing \(A\) or \(B\) of out scope of this PR.

**Conditions and limits:**

- PR2833 preserves separate historical migration, Confirmed-only sync, date/timestamp meanings, and optional-field alternatives. Naming evolves through priceDate to settlementDate. The final comment defers optional-forever versus mandatory-plus-migration to a later decision. ## R-3610 — FX daily-price conversion separates missing prior rate from mapping outcome and uses HALF_EVEN scale 2

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> marketdata-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/marketdata/impl/entities/instrument/processors/InstrumentMarketDataEventProcessorForMultiCcy.scala; PR 2600: removes failing when fx rate is not present for instrument price calculation in another ccy

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Nit: This log doesn’t feel right, cuz now we club the case when fxRateToUse is None, and then case when `.map(fxRateToUse => { blah } `produces None. I know it’s not possible for that map to produce None, but still :stuck_out_tongue: 
> 
> ‌
> 
> Maybe like this is better?
> 
> ```
> convertedDailyPrices = sortedDailyPrices.flatMap { dailyPrice =>
>   fxRates
>     .filterNot(_._1.isAfter(dailyPrice.priceDate))
>     .sortBy(_._1.toEpochDay)
>     .lastOption match {
>       case None =>
>         log.error(s"unable to find the fx rate [$instrumentCcy|$targetCcy] for the date [${dailyPrice.priceDate}], skipping for the date")
>         None
> 
>       case Some(fxRateToUse) =>
>         val convertedPrice = (dailyPrice.value * fxRateToUse._2).setScale(2, RoundingMode.HALF_EVEN)
>         Some(DailyPrice(businessDate = dailyPrice.businessDate, priceDate = dailyPrice.priceDate, priceCcy = targetCcy, value = convertedPrice))
>     }
> }
> ```
> 
> ‌
